results.correct_value: Glacier plus Class 3 scrambling for the usual line (a steep snow pitch then a scramble to the top); an all-rock line up the summit pinnacle is about Class 4. No 5.x move is on record — the 5.7/5.3 figures in pro_tips and watch_out belong to the Mount Olympus West Peak summit block, not Mount Tom.
results.evidence: Wikipedia's peak article gives the easiest route as glacier + Class 3 scrambling. A 2004 cascadeclimbers trip report (Olympus & Tom) says most parties climb a steep snow pitch then scramble to the summit pinnacle, while the author took an all-rock line of roughly 220 ft of 4th class, soloed. Search results attribute the '5.7 chimney vs 5.4 either side' description to the Olympus summit block, and no source gives any 5th-class move on Tom. rock_grade/pitch_detail 'Class 3' and the 'Class 3-4' range in route prose both fit; only the 5.7/5.3 claims are wrong.

results.evidence: The Forest Service trailhead page gives the Upper Trailhead at 47.8561, -123.035621 (the pin's own coordinate); the USGS 1 m elevation service at that point reads 3,342 ft. WTA gives 3,010 ft of gain to a 6,260 ft high point, i.e. a start near 3,250 ft, and Wikipedia likewise gives a 3,010 ft rise from the trailhead. Only Gaia GPS gives 3,400 ft. Both independent measures put the trailhead nearer 3,300 than 3,400, matching the row's own waypoint and gain_ft.

results.correct_value: The summit is climbed from the col at the south end of Gray Wolf Ridge, northeast of the peak, then up the broken northeast ridge (pinnacles passed on their east side, ledges and small gullies, an exposed blade to the top): Class 3 with perhaps one short Class 4 step. From Royal Basin the col is reached by a brushy forest band, a talus tongue below the east face and a scree rib; from Baldy by following Gray Wolf Ridge south. There is no east/southeast-gully 'West Side' line, and no west-side forest approach.
results.evidence: A 2008 WTA trip report climbed from the lower Royal Basin camp: a slow 700 ft brushy forest band, a talus tongue below the complex east face, northwest up boulders and a scree ridge to the south end of Gray Wolf Ridge (col NE of Walkinshaw), 4-5 pinnacles passed on the east side with Class 3 moves on rotten shale, then the NE ridge through ledges and gullies to an airy blade and the summit; it also notes others reach the same NE col along Gray Wolf Ridge. A 2023 cascadeclimbers report (Gray Wolf Ridge to Walkinshaw, 'Standard') climbed from the col south of South Gray Wolf: mostly exposed Class 3 with maybe one small 4th-class section, descending to the Royal Basin trail. Wikipedia gives Class 3 via Gray Wolf Ridge. The row's itinerary day 2 already describes this NE-ridge blade line; the approach/waypoints/baseFinding/beta/pitch_detail are rewritten to match (pins not moved).

patches.find: Aim for the prominent talus tongue and gully system on Walkinshaw's east/southeast side — this is the 'West Side' class-3 scramble route. Ascend the loose, blocky gully (described firsthand as 'rotten Olympic shale' — notably looser than typical Cascades granite) with care, then follow class 2-3 terrain along the upper ridge, including a few short class-3 moves past steepened pinnacles, to the small (~10-ft-diameter) rocky summit at 7,378 ft.
patches.replace: Aim for the prominent talus tongue below Walkinshaw's broken east face, then climb northwest over boulders and a bare scree rib to the col at the south end of Gray Wolf Ridge, northeast of the peak. From the col, skirt several steepening pinnacles on their east side with Class 3 moves on rotten shale (far looser than typical Cascades granite), then follow the northeast ridge through ledges and small gullies to an exposed blade of rock and the small (~10-ft-diameter) rocky summit at 7,378 ft — Class 3 overall, with perhaps one short Class 4 step.
